why: The break-even exists (jaw-soft 796 at ×1.30, sole-left/right 852) but the sourced $0.50–5.00 moulded-piece band was quoted for small injection-moulded rigid parts; no soft-tool or LSR piece price was sourced, and the §2.4 note already says a moulded version of this geometry is a redesign, not a re-quote.
what_settles_it: One quote for a silicone or LSR tool and piece price on jaw-soft and sole-left at 1,000 off. The playbook already names the silicone route (ML source, $500–3,000 per tool, 20–30 pulls) but has no piece price for it.

what: Which of the three shipped ST25R3916 packages the Microduck actually carries (UFQFPN32 5.000 x 5.000 x 0.550 Active, VFQFPN32 5.000 x 5.000 x 0.900 NRND, WLCSP36 3.213 x 3.203 x 0.590 Active)
why: the board that carries the chip is Pollen's, and it is unpublished. All three packages are now measured off DS12484 Rev 8 §6 (Tables 134/135/136, pp.150-155 of 160) so whichever is chosen has its numbers; nothing in the datasheet says which one this product uses.
what_settles_it: one photograph of the board, or a BOM line for it. A 5 mm square QFN and a 3.2 mm CSP are told apart by eye at any resolution that shows the chip.

what: The land PATTERN a board should etch for the LSM6DSV16X LGA-14L
why: the mechanical drawing (Figure 33, p.175 of DS13510 Rev 4) gives the package's own lands — 14 lands, pitch 0.5, 0.25 ±0.05 x 0.475 ±0.05 — and its own note sends a reader to ST technical note TN0018 for the land pattern and soldering, which is a different document and is not in this folder.
what_settles_it: fetching ST TN0018 into ce-parts/lsm6dsv16x and hashing it in PROVENANCE.json, the same way the datasheet is.

what: The five head folders (top-head-shell, bottom-head-shell, face-part, eye-ring, jaw) FAIL on out/head/front_fit.json — a ledgered artifact re-measured with no later row naming it
why: the artifact belongs to lane A, which regenerated it after those rows were written. The ledger is append-only and the last row's hash is the one checked, so nothing this lane can do inside the five folders closes it, and editing a row would be the wrong repair.
what_settles_it: lane A appending one row per folder for the new front_fit.json run. SHELF-STATUS.html §1 lists all five with that remedy, read out of the checker run rather than typed.

what: Whether a ref that was PASS at the 2026-09-02 snapshot is still PASS today
why: out/laneT/shelf-before.json was written by a generator that named only not-PASS refs — its totals say 59 checked and it carries 40 rows — so a ref PASS then and PASS now appears in neither file.
what_settles_it: nothing retroactive; the current generator names PASS refs, so the next before/after comparison will not have this asymmetry. The page states the limit rather than papering over it.

what: TRIAD.md's ledger `kind` vocabulary has no term for a dimension read off a vendor's mechanical drawing
why: bin/triad accepts sim|bench|field|standard|use|failure|export. A first attempt with kind 'dimension' was FAILED by the checker as an unknown kind and corrected to 'standard' before ever being committed — nothing append-only was rewritten — but 'standard' is a poor fit for a dimensional reading.
what_settles_it: a decision on TRIAD.md's ledger schema, which is a workshop-wide contract and not this repo's to change unilaterally. Both rows carry a kind_note saying exactly this.

what: Turnkey ASSEMBLY price for P1 and P2 at 3 / 100 / 1000 boards
why: Both fabs that gave a bare-board price quote bare board only. The two that advertise assembly publish a floor with no BOM attached — JLCPCB 'PCB Assembly From $8.00', PCBWay '$29 free shipping for 1-20pcs assembly' — and both instant-quote engines are JavaScript that WebFetch does not run (pcbway.com/orderonline.aspx, jlcpcb.com/quote, seeedstudio.com/fusion_pcb.html all recorded as blocked with the reason).
what_settles_it: A written quotation against the shipped bom.csv and positions.csv. The request is drafted in RFQ.html for all three fabs and has not been sent.

what: A second fab for P3 that will build a 45.8000 x 4.6000 mm board AND name ENIG on the order
why: OSH Park is measured-refused: both its service pages publish a minimum board size of 0.25 in (6.35 mm) square, against this board's 4.6000 mm short axis — short by 1.7500 mm. AdvancedPCB's $33 Each Special clears every published restriction but specifies lead-free HAL and only PERMITS ENIG at the fab's option, which is permission, not a specification, and this board is a sliding spring contact where a HASL pad cold-flows and oxidises.
what_settles_it: A quotation from JLCPCB — its published minimum board size is 3 x 3 mm and it lists ENIG on this process — or any fab that will price the board (or its array) with ENIG named on the order. Letter drafted, not sent.

what: The NP-F spring contact part for P3, and the 4.000 mm contact pitch it lands on
why: There is no identified bought part for the contacts at all: no manufacturer, no part number. Sony publishes no NP-F terminal drawing; the only public description found names the three terminals '+', 'C', '-' and gives no dimension. The 4.000 mm pitch is DERIVED — the 12.000 mm window measured in power_support.stl divided into three cells — and footprint P1 is marked UNCONFIRMED in the board's own bom.csv.
what_settles_it: A caliper across a physical NP-F550 pack. Nothing else does.

what: Whether OSH Park bills the bounding rectangle or the routed outline
why: Neither service page says. The bounding rectangle is used throughout (3.022506 and 1.364003 sq in), so every OSH Park number on P1 and P2 is a CEILING — by at most $0.0834 per set of three on P1.
what_settles_it: One sentence from OSH Park; it is asked in that supplier's RFQ letter.

what: Prices for five lines that carry none at all
why: B13 microphone(s) — nothing is known, not the part, type, count or placement, so there is no URL to try. B15 camera-in-use LED — placement is a mechanical and regulatory question, not a price one.
